rationale: A defensible additive composite of the archive's two best conditioners with an honest, correct claim that the outer RANK only reshapes the FMB regressor, but it is incremental recombination and the act/at leg already carried a wrong-signed FMB slope (-0.456), so the summed conditioner may dilute rather than repair the cross-sectional evidence.

target_name: Non Cash Current Asset Backing Test
rationale: The cash-versus-operating-current-asset decomposition is a legitimate diagnostic question, but as written it is a single-term substitution into an already-evaluated gen-2 signal whose likely outcome (a somewhat attenuated version of the same alpha) will not discriminate cleanly; running act/at and che/at as separate conditioners, or including the cash leg explicitly, would actually identify the driver.

This is a one-term benchmark swap on the weak gen-2 "Depreciation Lagging Asset Growth" signal (fmb 0.89, ls_talpha 2.35), and swapping the asset-growth confound for a sales-growth confound merely trades one known growth anomaly for another while leaving the noisy year-over-year dp growth term intact.

Sales-to-price is a genuinely different valuation leg that admits loss-makers and the loss-maker coverage argument is sound, but this is now the third instance of the same "hold the dp-deviation conditioner fixed and swap the multiple" template (ib-yield, ebitda-yield, now sale-yield), so its marginal information about the mechanism is modest.

target_name: Own History Cheapness With Verifiable Assets
rationale: TS_RANK of EBITDA/price over five annual observations is dominated by the price path and is therefore largely a repackaged long-horizon (De Bondt–Thaler) reversal signal rather than a new valuation dimension, and a 5-point discrete rank is a coarse, high-turnover value leg that will make the interaction hard to interpret.

target_name: Unit Cost Stability Within Cheap Firms
rationale: Gross-margin volatility is an established earnings-quality construct but has not been tested in this archive, it sits entirely above the accrual line so it is mechanically distinct from the failed earnings-versus-cash-volatility test, and the expression's sign convention (NEG of volatility) correctly matches the stated hypothesis.
